$comment: The registry of what exists, in which language, at what version. Read by tools/parity-check.mjs, which DISCOVERS languages from the repository rather than trusting this list — a hand-maintained list is exactly how a fifth copy of a version number goes three releases stale while the test written to catch that drift covers only four.
kit_note: The kit version names a SET tested together. It is not a version any package carries. Packages version independently — see docs/decisions/0001-versioning.md — and the kit does the compatibility-matrix job with one number instead of N squared.
$mirrors_comment: Units we have COMMITTED to keeping in step. The existence check FAILS when one is missing from a language that is required to have it. This is the half a conformance corpus cannot do: a fixture table compares two implementations and reports that they disagree, but it can never fail on ABSENCE, because a missing mirror has nothing to run the rows against. Drift and existence are different mechanisms and this repository ships both.
$deferred_comment: Units present in the reference that the ports deliberately do NOT have yet. Listed so the drift report can tell a decision apart from an oversight — an unlisted absence is drift and gets reported; a listed one is the plan.

deferred.reason: Out of the vertical slice. Tools can be declared and tool calls parsed, but the multi-step execution loop, approvals and concurrency are a much larger surface and porting them before the mapping patterns settled would have replicated whatever is wrong with them.
Present in the PORTS and absent from the reference, which is the unusual direction. particle-academy/prism can serialise its value objects and cannot read them back; see finding F-4.
Deliberately deferred. Telemetry is Laravel-event-shaped in the reference and a port should not inherit that shape without a decision about what the equivalent is.
Deferred with telemetry: the Thread contract is one method, but its value is in the Eloquent/storage integrations around it.
